tagline: Four miles from Bar Harbor by crow, forty-five by car.
intro: Out of Hancock, US 1 runs east through Sullivan, whose harbor looks straight across Frenchman Bay to Mount Desert Island. Then Route 186 turns off and makes a half-loop down the Gouldsboro coast, through Winter Harbor and Birch Harbor to Prospect Harbor, among fishing villages where lobstering and clamming carry on.

Bar Harbor is four miles off as the crow flies and 45 by road, and only about one Acadia visitor in ten makes the trip around. The name Schoodic is thought to come from a Passamaquoddy word for the burned place.

moments.title: Sullivan
moments.text: Granite quarried here was shipped as far as London and Hong Kong, and the Old Granite Store at the head of the harbor is built of the local stone.

moments.title: Schoodic Peninsula
moments.text: Past Winter Harbor a one-way loop road takes the park's quiet side around a granite shore laced with volcanic dikes, under 440-foot Schoodic Head.

moments.title: Prospect Harbor Point Light
moments.text: Lit in 1850, switched off in 1859 as not needed, lit again in 1870, and rebuilt in 1891 as the shingled wooden tower still working the harbor.

practical: The Acadia loop road at Schoodic Point is one-way, about 7 miles.
